guides.title: How this vault works
guides.summary: What the folders, tags and buttons on this site mean.
steps: Open the Files tab and pick a folder: ROMs, Recoveries, Root, Stock, Personal Vault or Utilities.
Use the chips inside a folder to narrow it down, for example one ROM family or only Drivers.
Read the status tag. Daily driver means I run it. Tested means it worked for me. Partial means it works with known bugs. Untested means I collected it but haven't tried it.
Read the badge. Official comes from the ROM's own team, Unofficial is a community build, and Port is made from another device's firmware.
Download opens the main file. Source opens the post where it was published. Extra buttons such as Changelog, XDA or Guide open the maintainer's own pages.
When a SHA-256 button is shown, copy it and compare it with the hash of your downloaded file.
warnings: Most files here are linked from their authors' own pages. Unless a file is tagged Daily driver or Tested, I haven't verified it myself.

guides.title: Before you flash anything
guides.summary: A checklist to run through before any flashing guide on this site.
prereqs: A Nord 2 and its exact model, DN2101 (India) or DN2103 (EU)
A PC with platform-tools (ADB and fastboot) and the MTK USB driver installed
A backup of everything you care about
steps: Open Settings, then About phone, and write down your model number (DN2101 or DN2103).
Back up photos, chats, authenticator codes and app data to a PC or cloud. Format-data steps erase internal storage.
Charge the phone to at least 60% so it can't power off during a flash.
Download only files made for your model and region, and read the maintainer's notes (for example whether a clean flash is required).
Verify the download when a SHA-256 is listed. On Windows run: certutil -hashfile <file> SHA256. On Linux or macOS run: sha256sum <file>. Then compare the two values.
Keep a stock OxygenOS package from the Stock folder on your PC so you can go back.
Connect the phone with USB debugging on and check that it appears when you run: adb devices
warnings: Flashing can brick the phone, void the warranty and erase your data. Read the BROM restore guide before you start so you know your way back.

guides.title: Choosing a custom ROM from the ROMs folder
guides.summary: How to read a ROM entry before you download it.
prereqs: A completed 'Before you flash anything' checklist
steps: Pick a ROM family with the chips (Evolution X, LineageOS, Lunaris-AOSP and so on) and look at its newest entry first.
Check the Android version and the badge. Official builds come from the ROM team, Unofficial builds from individual maintainers, and Ports are built from another phone's firmware.
Open the Changelog, Bugs and Notes buttons when a ROM has them, and read them before downloading.
Follow the ROM's own flashing guide when it has one (the OxygenOS 15 and ColorOS 15 ports do). Several maintainers say a clean flash is mandatory, so back up first.
Flash GApps only when the ROM post says so. For example the ArrowOS 12.1 post says GApps are needed for vanilla builds only.
Check the SHA-256 when it is listed, or the checksum file for DerpFest 13.
If something goes wrong, use the revert-to-stock guide.
warnings: These builds come from third-party maintainers. Their posts, changelogs and bug lists are the final word on how to install them.

guides.title: Revert from an AOSP custom ROM to stock
guides.summary: Go back to OxygenOS 11.3 from a custom ROM using ADB sideload.
prereqs: Platform-tools on your PC and the MTK USB driver installed
The OxygenOS 11.3 package for your model (EU DN2103 or IN DN2101) from the Stock folder
A backup, because formatting data erases the phone
The custom ROM's own recovery on the phone
steps: On the phone, open Settings, then About phone, and note the model.
Download the stock package for your model from the Stock folder.
On the PC open a terminal in the platform-tools folder.
Reboot the phone into the AOSP recovery and choose Apply Update, then Using ADB.
On the PC run: adb devices. The phone should be listed in sideload mode.
Run: adb sideload <package>.zip. The original post uses the file name oplus_ota_downgrade.zip.
If your custom ROM was based on DN2103 (EU) firmware, flash the EU stock ROM first.
When flashing is complete, format data in recovery and reboot to system.
Check Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, audio, camera and mobile data.
Optional: to relock the bootloader, once you are fully back on stock, run adb reboot bootloader and then fastboot flashing lock.
warnings: Do not lock the bootloader while a custom ROM or custom recovery is installed. The phone may refuse to boot.
guides.credit: Steps are from the OPN2-Dump channel.

guides.title: Switch from DN2103 to DN2101 firmware (India users, optional)
guides.summary: Move an EU-firmware Nord 2 to the Indian OxygenOS 11.3 build with a local install.
prereqs: A full backup, because this erases everything
The OxygenOS 11.3 IN package copied to the phone's internal storage
steps: Open Settings and turn off network access for the Software Update app so it can't push OTA updates meanwhile.
Enable Developer options by tapping the version number 5 to 6 times.
Open Software Update, tap the three dots and choose Local install.
Select the OxygenOS 11.3 IN ROM, install it and reboot.
If you want to relock the bootloader afterwards, reboot to the bootloader and run: fastboot flashing lock
warnings: Only lock the bootloader on a complete stock system.
guides.credit: Steps are from the OPN2-Dump channel.

guides.title: Restore BROM / fastboot (make the phone brick-proof)
guides.summary: Flash the preloader and lk files so a bad flash can be recovered.
prereqs: OxygenOS F.50 or lower with USB debugging on (tested on these builds)
The bulletproof_denniz.zip from the Utilities folder, extracted on your PC
Platform-tools and the MTK USB driver
steps: Extract all the files from the zip and open a terminal in that folder.
Run: adb reboot fastboot
Run: fastboot flash sda preloader_ufs_c01.img
Run: fastboot flash sdb preloader_ufs_c01.img
Run: fastboot flash lk lk_a20.bin
Run: fastboot flash lk2 lk2_a20.bin
Run: fastboot reboot
warnings: These commands overwrite the preloader and bootloader (lk) partitions. Use only the files from the zip, only on a Nord 2 (denniz), and do not unplug the phone during the flash.
guides.credit: The BROM bypass was discovered by @NishantKumar6342. The files are hosted on giovix92's SourceForge.

guides.title: Debloat with Shizuku and Canta (no root)
guides.summary: Remove system apps over wireless debugging without unlocking or rooting.
prereqs: Shizuku and Canta Debloater installed (both are in the Utilities folder)
A Wi-Fi connection, because wireless debugging needs it
steps: Enable Developer options by tapping the version number 5 to 6 times, then turn on Wireless debugging.
Open Shizuku and pair it with the phone, following the official Shizuku setup guide.
Start Shizuku and allow Canta Debloater to use it.
Open Canta and select only apps marked Recommended.
Tap Uninstall and confirm.
warnings: Only remove Recommended apps. Removing core system packages can crash or break the system.
guides.credit: Steps are from the OPN2-Dump channel.

intro: This is my personal vault for the OnePlus Nord 2 5G (codename denniz). It collects the firmware, recoveries, tools and extras I use or keep as backups, grouped into folders so you can find a file without scrolling through everything.

Nothing is hosted on this website. Each Download button points to the original source or to a post in my Telegram channel, and every entry shows who made it. The status tags show how much of it I have tested myself.
